messages:
maria: Hey all — seeing a spike in partial WS responses and a few customers report truncated streams. Any quick pointers where to pull the rollback logs and correlate traces?

ashwin: First place I check is the websocket consumer traces in Jaeger (service=runtime-ws). Look for spans with tag ws.chunk.partial=true. That usually points to the server-side generator dropping frames.

oliver: We also saw a pattern where nginx timeouts during upstream reconnects produced similar symptoms. Check the nginx error logs for  upstream timed out or 502s around the same time window.

maria: Good call — do we have a dashboard/panel that ties chunk latency to disconnects?

ashwin: Yeah, Grafana panel: /d/redwood/streaming-observability?panelId=7 (Chunk latency histogram) and panelId=12 (WS disconnect rate). Use the time range and then click a trace link on the histogram to open Jaeger.

oliver: For logs, Datadog query that helped me:
```
logs("service:runtime-ws AND @ws.partial:true") | timeseries(avg:duration)
```
Filter by client.ip or request_id to correlate with traces.

maria: Any quick way to find the "rollback" deploys that might've coincided?

deploy-bot: New deploy: runtime-ws v1.23.4 -> v1.23.5 (sha: ab12cd) at 2026-02-18T15:14:03Z
deploy-bot: Rolled back to v1.23.4 at 2026-02-18T15:28:11Z (rollback initiated by @oliver)

sre-oncall: If there's a rollback, look in the releases table in the release-metadata service. Query: `SELECT * FROM releases WHERE service='runtime-ws' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-02-18 15:00' AND '2026-02-18 15:40' ORDER BY created_at DESC;`

ashwin: To tie a specific client session -> trace, match websocket connect.websocket_id with trace tag trace.websocket_id. Our trace injection adds `x-trace-id` in the response headers; if you have a client-side trace id, paste it in Jaeger search.

maria: I'm looking at Grafana now — I can see a cluster of chunk latencies at ~15:16. Clicking one point opens Jaeger but there are many short spans. What's the best filter to find partial-frame errors in logs?

oliver: Use this filtered LogQL / Datadog pattern to catch the error type we use for partial frames: `@msg: \"incomplete_frame\" OR @error: \"partial_frame\"` and include `@request_id` so you can group. In Datadog you can do:
```
logs("service:runtime-ws AND (incomplete_frame OR partial_frame)") | group_by(@request_id) | top(50, avg_duration)
```

sre-oncall: Also check the connection lifecycle metric: `runtime.ws.connections_state_change{state:disconnect, reason:*}` in our metrics namespace. If reason=backend_reset or upstream_timeout that's a hint to look at upstream infra.

maria: I found a trace with span `ws.send_chunk` that has attribute `chunk_size=0` and a sibling span error `io.write: broken pipe`. Sounds like client disconnected mid-stream. Is there a known issue where prefix cache invalidation triggers empty chunks?

ashwin: Not common, but possible when prefix cache eviction happens mid-response and the generator falls back to streaming from disk which can be slower; if client has strict timeout you'll see broken pipe. Check the prefix-cache evictions metric: `runtime.cache.prefix_evictions` around that time.

oliver: If you want to pull raw connection logs from the node, you can run on the host: `sudo journalctl -u runtime-ws -o short-iso --since \"2026-02-18 15:10\" --until \"2026-02-18 15:20\" | grep -E \"request_id|incomplete_frame|write error\"`

maria: Perfect. One more ask — can someone tweak the alert to surface a sample trace link in the alert body? Right now it only shows counts.

sre-oncall: Yep — I can add a field to the Datadog monitor to attach the top offending trace link (we have a mapping function) for the next alert. Will open a small PR.

oliver: Quick note for the runbook: when you see partial frames + broken pipe, checklist: correlate deploys -> check prefix cache evictions -> check nginx upstream timeouts -> grab sample trace id -> collect host journal logs.

maria: Thanks all — I'll follow the checklist and post any traces here. If I find a consistent request_id I'll @oliver for a deeper look. :thumbsup:
